purpose: Give callisto consumers a working, documented mechanism that places CI-built native binary artifacts (napi-rs .node files, maturin wheels) into their platform-stub package directories before `callisto publish` runs, closing the gap between `callisto matrix`'s output and a working end-to-end release, with artifact names that stay unique when multiple packages in one workspace share a target triple.
scope: Two changes. (1) Rust: `crates/callisto-graph/src/matrix.rs`'s `artifact_name_for_triple(triple: &str) -> String` is replaced with `artifact_name_for_package_platform(package_name: &str, platform: &str, arch: &str, abi: Option<&str>) -> String`, which first sanitizes `package_name` by replacing every `/` character with `-` (because `actions/upload-artifact` forbids `/` in artifact names, and an npm scoped package name such as `@scope/addon` legitimately contains one), then returns `format!("{package_name}-{platform}-{arch}")` when `abi` is `None`, or `format!("{package_name}-{platform}-{arch}-{abi}")` when `abi` is `Some`, using the sanitized `package_name`. This matches napi-rs's own published-platform-package and recommended-CI-artifact-name convention (`<name>-<platform>-<arch>[-<abi>]`, e.g. `@scope/addon-darwin-arm64` on the npm registry becomes artifactName `@scope-addon-darwin-arm64`) rather than the raw Rust target triple. `build_platform_target` (already receiving `package_name` as a parameter) calls `triple_to_role(triple)` to destructure `(platform, arch, abi)` and passes those -- not the raw triple string -- into `artifact_name_for_package_platform`. This embeds the already-workspace-unique `package_name` (a value `PlatformTarget` already carries, sourced from each package's own identity) into `artifactName`, so two different packages declaring the same triple no longer produce colliding CI artifact names. (2) GitHub Actions: extends `.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml`'s existing `callisto-orchestrate` composite-action step -- within the block already guarded by `[[ -n "$INPUT_PUBLISH" && "$INPUT_PUBLISH" != "false" ]]` (action.yml:167), immediately after `NATIVE_MATRIX` is computed, adds a placement loop that downloads each `nativeMatrix` entry's artifact by `artifactName` (pinned to the current run via `$GITHUB_RUN_ID`) and places its contents into `packageDir`. Also updates `docs/specs/callisto-matrix.md` §6.2, updates `docs/specs/callisto-matrix.md` §4's artifact-naming-convention section to replace its unsanitized `@scope/addon-darwin-arm64` illustration with the sanitized `@scope-addon-darwin-arm64` and a sentence stating that `packageName` has every `/` replaced with `-` before formatting, and corrects `ARCHITECTURE.md` §12's broken example workflow.
non_goals: Extending PlatformTargetKind to Java/JNI or .NET native-AOT targets -- a separate, later concern; this spec only routes the two kinds PlatformTargetKind already supports (Napi, Maturin).
Prebuilt Rust CLI binaries distributed as GitHub Release assets ("Tier 2") -- a separate, related, deferred future spec.
Homebrew tap formula generation/distribution -- deferred by the maintainer as a possible separate future tool.
Go binary distribution -- already an existing non-goal per docs/specs/callisto-matrix.md §8, not being revisited here.

A generic callisto-build-action that dispatches the actual per-platform build (napi build --platform --release, etc.) -- callisto-matrix.md §7's secondary/optional proposal. This spec covers only placement of an already-built, correctly-named artifact; the build step itself is the consumer's own responsibility.

Validating the content of a downloaded artifact (e.g. confirming a .node file is well-formed, or that it is actually a valid binary for its target triple). The placement step moves whatever files gh run download retrieves into packageDir; content correctness is the build job's responsibility and surfaces later, at publish or install time, not at placement.

Adding a new required input to callisto-action to opt into placement. Placement is driven entirely by whether nativeMatrix is a non-empty array -- consumers with no native platform targets see zero behavior change.

Implementing the nonexistent callisto publish-target Rust CLI subcommand referenced by ARCHITECTURE.md §12's status note (line 447). That subcommand is not needed for this requirement and is not built by this spec; the status note's reference to it (alongside Java/.NET native-AOT discovery) remains accurate and is deliberately left in place -- only the example workflow's own code block, which currently invokes the nonexistent subcommand directly and dereferences nonexistent matrix.os/matrix.package/matrix.target-as-scalar fields, is corrected.

Guaranteeing that a binary placed at packageDir by this step is picked up and included in callisto publish's registry upload output (npm tarball, PyPI wheel, etc.). That round-trip guarantee is owned by whatever spec governs callisto publish's own native-binary packaging logic (crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/publish.rs) -- this spec's guarantee ends at the file being present on disk at packageDir before publish begins.

Handling malformed or invalid-JSON nativeMatrix values within callisto-action's own in-step placement loop. NATIVE_MATRIX (action.yml:164) is produced and consumed entirely within one shell step under `set -o pipefail`, with `jq` already validating JSON syntax (and failing the step via `|| { echo "::error::callisto matrix failed"; exit 1; }`) before the placement loop added by this spec ever reads the value -- malformed JSON cannot reach this specific loop by construction. This does not apply to a consumer's own custom multi-job pipeline built against callisto-matrix.md §6.2's standalone reference snippet, where nativeMatrix genuinely crosses a job-output boundary; that snippet's own error handling is out of scope for this spec beyond the run-id pin AC-011 requires.

Handling a missing (absent-key) or null artifactName/packageDir field on an otherwise-valid nativeMatrix entry. crates/callisto-model/src/matrix.rs's PlatformTarget declares both fields as plain `String` (not `Option<String>`), so serde can never serialize a missing or null value for either field into the JSON callisto matrix emits.

Preserving the exact literal string format `native-{triple}` (the raw-triple format, with no package-name component, from before this spec's own change) or the intermediate two-segment `native-{package_name}-{triple}` format (a shape this spec never actually implemented) as a stable, versioned contract of callisto matrix's JSON output. This spec's actual implemented change makes artifactName equal to `<sanitized packageName>-{platform}-{arch}[-{abi}]` (packageName with every `/` replaced with `-`) -- napi-rs's own published-package/CI-artifact-name convention, derived from `triple_to_role`'s platform/arch/abi decomposition rather than the raw triple -- to fix the collision defect while matching napi-rs tooling's own expectations. A consumer that hardcoded any prior format rather than treating artifactName as an opaque per-entry correlation token (its documented purpose) will observe a different string. No config override for this naming scheme is provided -- package_name is already sourced from the package's own identity, which is already user-configurable through the normal manifest name field; a separate artifact-naming override would duplicate that control for no benefit, since the artifact name is a CI-internal correlation id, never published or user-facing.

Guarding against two distinct packageName values that sanitize to an identical artifactName under the `/`-to-`-` replacement (e.g. a package literally named `a/b` and a separate package literally named `a-b` in the same workspace, both declaring the same triple) -- a theoretical collision this spec's AC-001/AC-002 uniqueness guarantee does not additionally cover, since that guarantee rests on packageName distinctness before sanitization, not after. This is not additionally guarded against because it requires two workspace packages whose names differ only in whether a literal `/` or `-` occupies the same character position -- already vanishingly narrow given each ecosystem's own name-character constraints (an npm scoped name uses `/` exactly once, as the mandatory `@scope/name` separator; Cargo and PyPI package names disallow `/` entirely, so a Rust or Python packageName can never collide this way with anything) -- and because artifactName is already documented above as an opaque CI-internal correlation token, not a uniqueness-guaranteed namespace independent of the packageName a maintainer chooses.

api_surface.name: artifact_name_for_package_platform
api_surface.signature: pub(crate) fn artifact_name_for_package_platform(package_name: &str, platform: &str, arch: &str, abi: Option<&str>) -> String
api_surface.description: Replaces `artifact_name_for_triple(triple: &str) -> String`. First sanitizes `package_name` by replacing every `/` with `-` (actions/upload-artifact forbids `/` in artifact names, and an npm scoped package name such as `@scope/addon` legitimately contains one), then returns `format!("{package_name}-{platform}-{arch}")` with the sanitized name when `abi` is `None`, or `format!("{package_name}-{platform}-{arch}-{abi}")` when `abi` is `Some`, matching napi-rs's own published-platform-package and recommended-CI-artifact-name convention (`<name>-<platform>-<arch>[-<abi>]`). `build_platform_target` (crates/callisto-graph/src/matrix.rs:138-155), which already receives `package_name` as a parameter, calls `triple_to_role(triple)` (crates/callisto-graph/src/napi.rs) to destructure `(platform, arch, abi)` and passes those values -- not the raw triple string -- into this function when constructing `PlatformTarget.artifact_name`.

api_surface.name: callisto-action native artifact placement loop
api_surface.signature: New shell logic inside `.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml`'s existing `callisto-orchestrate` composite step, placed inside the `[[ -n "$INPUT_PUBLISH" && "$INPUT_PUBLISH" != "false" ]]` guard (action.yml:167) immediately after `NATIVE_MATRIX` is computed (action.yml:164-165) and before `callisto plan-publish`/publish executes.
api_surface.description: Feeds `NATIVE_MATRIX` through process substitution, not a pipe -- `while IFS= read -r ENTRY; do ... done < <(printf '%s' "$NATIVE_MATRIX" | jq -c '.[]')` -- matching the existing pattern used for the releases loop at action.yml:219, so an `exit 1` inside the loop body terminates the step itself, not a subshell. For each ENTRY: extracts `ARTIFACT=$(echo "$ENTRY" | jq -r '.artifactName')` and `DIR_RAW=$(echo "$ENTRY" | jq -r '.packageDir')`; sets `DIR` to `.` when `DIR_RAW` is the empty string (the real value `packageDir` takes for a workspace-root package, per crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/matrix.rs:34-39), otherwise `DIR=$DIR_RAW`; runs `mkdir -p "$DIR"` explicitly; then runs `gh run download "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --name "$ARTIFACT" --dir "$DIR" || { echo "::error::failed to download artifact '$ARTIFACT' for placement into '$DIR' within run $GITHUB_RUN_ID"; exit 1; }`. Runs once per array element, in array order. Skipped entirely (loop body never executes) when `NATIVE_MATRIX` is `[]`.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given two distinct packages in the same workspace that each declare the same platform target triple (e.g. both declare aarch64-apple-darwin), `callisto matrix --format json`'s output contains two distinct entries for that triple -- one per package -- and their `artifactName` values differ, each shaped `<sanitized packageName>-<platform>-<arch>` (or `<sanitized packageName>-<platform>-<arch>-<abi>` when the triple carries an abi, e.g. a musl or gnu linux triple), where `<sanitized packageName>` is that entry's own packageName with every `/` character replaced with `-`, and `<platform>`/`<arch>`/`<abi>` are the same platform/arch/abi values that entry's own `platform`/`arch`/`abi` fields report. For example, packages `pkg-a` and `pkg-b` both declaring `aarch64-apple-darwin` produce `artifactName` values `pkg-a-darwin-arm64` and `pkg-b-darwin-arm64` -- distinct because packageName differs, containing no raw triple substring (e.g. no `aarch64-apple-darwin` appearing anywhere in the result), no vendor component (e.g. `apple`, `pc`, `unknown`), and no fixed `native-` prefix. Separately, a package named `@scope/addon` declaring `aarch64-apple-darwin` produces `artifactName` `@scope-addon-darwin-arm64` -- the packageName's `/` replaced with `-` -- containing no `/` anywhere in the result.

Given the same two-packages-one-triple scenario as AC-001, `.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml`'s `NATIVE_MATRIX` computation (which pipes callisto matrix's output through `unique_by(.artifactName)`) retains both packages' entries rather than collapsing them to one, because their artifactName values are now distinct.

Given a workflow run where N per-platform build jobs each upload an artifact via actions/upload-artifact using the exact artifactName string from that platform's callisto matrix --format json entry, and the callisto-orchestrate step's placement loop (placed inside the `[[ -n "$INPUT_PUBLISH" && "$INPUT_PUBLISH" != "false" ]]` guard, not merely somewhere after NATIVE_MATRIX computation) executes: after the step completes, each of the N artifacts' downloaded file contents are present under the corresponding packageDir path relative to the working directory (with the directory having been created via the loop's own mkdir -p if it did not already exist), and this placement completes before the step's callisto plan-publish/publish invocation begins.

Given nativeMatrix is [] (no native platform-target packages in the workspace) and INPUT_PUBLISH is non-empty and not the literal string "false" (so the guard at action.yml:167 is entered), the placement loop body never executes (zero gh run download invocations) because NATIVE_MATRIX's parsed array is empty, and the step proceeds directly to callisto plan-publish/publish exactly as it did before this change. Given INPUT_PUBLISH is unset or the literal string "false", the placement loop is never reached regardless of nativeMatrix's contents, because the loop is placed inside that same guard.

Given a nativeMatrix entry whose packageDir field is the empty string (the value produced for a workspace-root package whose manifest has no parent directory component), the placement loop sets DIR to "." before calling mkdir -p and gh run download --dir, and the corresponding artifact's contents are placed directly under the working directory rather than the step failing or attempting mkdir -p with an empty path.

Given a nativeMatrix entry whose artifactName was never uploaded within the current workflow run ($GITHUB_RUN_ID) -- including the case where an artifact with that exact name exists in a different, older, or unrelated workflow run in the same repository -- the loop's `gh run download "$GITHUB_RUN_ID" --name "$ARTIFACT" --dir "$DIR"` invocation exits non-zero because the run-id pins the lookup to the current run only, the `|| { ...; exit 1; }` clause terminates the step (not merely a pipeline subshell) before reaching callisto plan-publish/publish, and the step's log output names the specific missing artifactName and the DIR value (post `.`-normalization where applicable) that download attempt was targeting.

ARCHITECTURE.md §12's example workflow code block (the fenced code block following the "Zero-Config GitHub Actions Workflow Pattern" heading) contains no occurrence of the string "callisto publish-target" anywhere within it; the status note above the heading (naming Java/JNI, .NET native-AOT, and the callisto publish-target subcommand as unimplemented) is unchanged and still present.

ARCHITECTURE.md §12's example workflow's build job uses the namespaced GitHub Actions matrix form matching callisto-matrix.md §6.1's own documented consumption pattern: `strategy.matrix.target` is set to `${{ fromJson(needs.matrix.outputs.nativeMatrix) }}`, and every per-entry field is dereferenced under the `matrix.target.` prefix -- `runs-on: ${{ matrix.target.hostRunner }}`, plus `matrix.target.triple`, `matrix.target.artifactName`, and `matrix.target.packageDir` in the build/upload steps -- with each of these four resolving to a real field on PlatformTarget's camelCase JSON serialization (hostRunner, triple, artifactName, packageDir). The block contains no bare, non-namespaced `matrix.os` or `matrix.package` reference (neither is a real field under any prefix), and contains no use of `matrix.target` as a plain scalar value (e.g. `${{ matrix.target }}` alone) -- `matrix.target` appears only as the namespace prefix for a specific field.

ARCHITECTURE.md §12's example workflow code block contains all of: (a) a build job's `actions/upload-artifact` step with `name: ${{ matrix.target.artifactName }}`; (b) a release job step invoking `./.github/actions/callisto-action` with `publish: true`; (c) a comment block immediately preceding that callisto-action step containing both the substring "uploaded artifact into its packageDir" and the substring "automatically inside this step" -- documenting that placement happens automatically within the action, not via a separate consumer-authored step. The block contains no consumer-authored `gh run download` invocation or other literal placement step, consistent with AC-010 and AC-011.

A consumer workflow that already uses callisto-action for publishing and adds only a matrix-driven build job (per docs/specs/callisto-matrix.md §6.1's nativeMatrix consumption pattern) uploading artifacts named per artifactName, with no additional bash, composite action, or script authored by the consumer to perform placement, ends with the callisto-orchestrate step having invoked gh run download once per nativeMatrix entry and each entry's artifact contents present at that entry's packageDir (post `.`-normalization) -- with no requirement on this spec's part that callisto publish itself subsequently succeeds, per this spec's non-goal on the publish-side packaging round-trip.

docs/specs/callisto-matrix.md §6.2's standalone reference snippet (for consumers building their own custom multi-job pipeline outside callisto-action, where nativeMatrix genuinely crosses a `needs.<job>.outputs.nativeMatrix` job-output boundary) is updated to pin the download to `$GITHUB_RUN_ID` and to `mkdir -p "$DIR"` before calling `gh run download`, and §6.2 gains an explicit note stating that consumers using callisto-action for publishing do not need to write this snippet themselves -- callisto-action performs equivalent placement automatically, in-step, once nativeMatrix is non-empty and publish is enabled.

docs/specs/callisto-matrix.md §4 ("Artifact naming convention") contains no occurrence of the unsanitized string `@scope/addon-darwin-arm64` anywhere in the section; the section's illustration of the napi-rs convention instead shows the sanitized form `@scope-addon-darwin-arm64`, and the section contains a sentence stating that `packageName` has every `/` character replaced with `-` before formatting.

revision_note: Abandoned: the callisto-action placement loop shipped in #15 and was removed in #39 with no replacement; only the package-scoped artifact naming (AC-001) remains.
reasoning: Verified directly against live source: crates/callisto-graph/src/matrix.rs's artifact_name_for_package_platform (lines 36-52) sanitizes package_name via .replace('/', "-") before formatting, and the test artifact_name_for_package_platform_sanitizes_scoped_npm_package_name (line 787) confirms artifact_name_for_package_platform("@scope/addon", "darwin", "arm64", None) == "@scope-addon-darwin-arm64" with no '/' in the result. AC-001, api_surface[0].description, and scope's Rust-change sentence were rewritten to state the sanitization rule. Checked AC-002 through AC-011 individually: none quote or depend on the exact artifactName string shape besides AC-001; AC-002 depends only on distinctness surviving through unique_by(.artifactName), which sanitization does not undermine in the general case. Chose non_goals over a new acceptance criterion for the residual a/b-vs-a-b collision because guarding against it would require either rejecting '/'-containing non-scoped names outright (a breaking behavior change out of this spec's scope) or a more elaborate collision-detection mechanism neither requested nor evidenced as needed by any real workspace; the existing artifactName-is-an-opaque-token framing already carried in non_goals covers the same reasoning, so this is additive to an established pattern rather than a new precedent. (5) Fixed per canon:auditor's FAIL verdict on round (4)'s draft. Auditor issue 1: direct inspection of docs/specs/callisto-matrix.md §4 (lines 198-224) showed its own artifact-naming-convention illustration still contains the unsanitized string `@scope/addon-darwin-arm64`, which round (4)'s sanitization correction makes factually wrong, and scope's doc-update sentence named only §6.2, not §4 -- an incomplete-section gap. Fixed by extending scope's documentation sentence to also cover §4's correction (unsanitized illustration replaced with `@scope-addon-darwin-arm64` plus a sanitization-rule sentence) and adding AC-012 requiring exactly that. Auditor issue 2: AC-001's parenthetical '(derived from the triple, not the triple string itself)' was self-contradictory on its face (a triple is already a string), giving testers no actual distinguishing predicate. Fixed by replacing it with '(derived via triple_to_role's structured platform/arch/abi decomposition, not by substring-slicing the raw triple string)', which states the real, testable distinction (structured decomposition via the existing triple_to_role function vs. ad hoc substring slicing). Round (5) fixes verified against docs/specs/callisto-matrix.md:203 (confirmed the exact stale string `@scope/addon-darwin-arm64` is present in §4's fenced example block) with no other occurrence elsewhere in the file. No further criteria depend on §4's content besides the new AC-012, since AC-001/AC-002/AC-003 etc. all reference callisto matrix's JSON output or action.yml behavior, not this markdown doc.
